questions.question_text: A personal loan of $\$18\,000$ charges $9\%$ p.a. compounded monthly with monthly repayments of $\$420$. Which recurrence relation models the loan balance $A_{n}$ after $n$ months?

options.why: Used the annual rate with the monthly $n$.
Added repayments instead of subtracting them from the loan balance.
Multiplied by the interest rate alone instead of the growth factor $1+r$.

questions.question_text: A debt of $\$6000$ has a monthly interest rate of $1\%$ ($r=0.01$) and monthly repayments of $\$250$. Which expression represents the balance $A_{2}$ after $2$ repayments?

options.why: Subtracted simple total repayments without compounding the first repayment.
Applied an extra power of the growth factor to the first repayment.
Used the annual rate with the monthly $n$.

questions.question_text: In the loan balance expansion $A_{n}=PV(1+r)^{n}-M(1+r)^{n-1}-M(1+r)^{n-2}-\dots-M$, what are the common ratio and number of terms of the repayment series $M+M(1+r)+\dots+M(1+r)^{n-1}$?

options.why: Confused the common ratio with the interest rate $r$ rather than $1+r$.
Counted the highest power $n-1$ instead of the total number of terms from $0$ to $n-1$.
Confused the common ratio with the first term $M$.

questions.solution_text:
The terms are $M(1+r)^{0}, M(1+r)^{1}, \dots, M(1+r)^{n-1}$.
Each term is multiplied by $1+r$, so the common ratio is $1+r$.
The powers range from $0$ to $n-1$, giving $n$ terms.

questions.question_text: A car loan of $\$22\,000$ incurs interest at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.005$) with monthly repayments of $\$500$. Which is the correct expanded expression for $A_{3}$?

options.why: Included four repayment terms instead of three for $A_3$.
Used the annual rate with the monthly $n$.
Treated repayments as a simple uncompounded lump sum.

questions.question_text: How does a reducing balance loan differ fundamentally from a flat-rate loan?

options.text: Interest on a reducing balance loan is charged only on the remaining balance each period, whereas a flat-rate loan charges interest on the original principal throughout.
A reducing balance loan charges simple interest while a flat-rate loan charges compound interest.
options.why: Inverted the interest types between flat-rate and reducing balance loans.

options.text: A reducing balance loan has repayments that increase each month.
options.why: Mistakenly claims repayments change rather than the interest component changing.

options.text: A reducing balance loan charges all interest at the end of the loan term.
options.why: Confused reducing balance loans with deferred interest loans.

questions.solution_text:
In a reducing balance loan, interest is calculated on the reducing unpaid principal.
In a flat-rate loan, interest is calculated on the initial principal for the entire loan duration.
Therefore, reducing balance loans charge less total interest over time.

questions.question_text: A loan of $\$14\,000$ charges interest at $7.8\%$ p.a. compounded half-yearly with half-yearly repayments of $\$1200$. What is the recurrence relation for the balance $A_{n}$?

options.why: Used the annual rate with the monthly $n$.
Added the repayments instead of subtracting them from the debt.
Divided the annual rate by 12 instead of 2 for half-yearly compounding.

questions.question_text: A borrower takes a loan of $\$40\,000$ at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($r=0.005$) and makes monthly repayments of $\$180$. What will happen to the loan balance $A_{n}$ over time?

options.text: The balance increases each month because the monthly repayment of $\$180$ is less than the first month's interest of $\$200$.
The balance decreases steadily to zero after approximately $222$ months.
options.why: Assumed repayments always pay off the loan regardless of the interest amount.

options.text: The balance remains constant at $\$40\,000$ every month.
options.why: Assumed the repayment exactly balances the monthly interest charge.

options.text: The loan is paid off in fewer than $100$ months due to compounding.
options.why: Mistakenly believed compounding accelerates loan payoff even when repayments are below interest.

questions.solution_text:
First month interest $=40\,000\times0.005=\$200$
$A_{1}=40\,000(1.005)-180=40\,200-180=\$40\,020$
Since the repayment is less than the interest added, the balance increases indefinitely.

questions.question_text: For a loan of $\$P$ at periodic interest rate $r$ with regular repayment $M$, if the borrower makes no repayment at the end of the first period but makes payment $M$ in all subsequent periods, what is the balance $A_{2}$?

options.why: Included a repayment in the first period when none was made.
Only compounded the principal for one period instead of two.
Subtracted two repayments without accounting for the skipped first payment.
